newsitem.title: USA: INSTANT VIEW - U.S. stocks seen lower after CPI.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - U.S. stocks seen lower after CPI.

text.p: U.S. stocks were seen opening lower on Thursday after a report on the April Consumer Price Index, analysts said. The following are their comments:
MICHAEL METZ, CHIEF INVESTMENT STRATEGIST AT OPPENHEIMER & CO:

-- The data "were a little bit disappointing. Even though the PPI can remain reassuring, the CPI is really going to present a problem, in my opinion. In my opinion, it is more than enough justification for the Fed to move next week."
The CPI rose 0.1 percent in April. Excluding food and energy, the index was up 0.3 percent. Economists had expected overall CPI to rise 0.1 percent and the core rate to rise 0.2 percent.

-- "The numbers were a tad disappointing. The core rates were up 0.3 percent and the projections were 0.2...It is hurting bonds. The stock market follows the bond market so if the bonds are hurt, the stocks are going to be weak."
JIM SOLLOWAY, DIRECTOR OF RESEARCH AT ARGUS RESEARCH:
-- "The top-line numbers look pretty much in line with expectations so that shouldn't have too much of an impact on how the markets trade today."
-- "Far more important right now is the weakness in the dollar and concern that the stock market at least is priced a little highly after the last several weeks of strong rallying."
-- Said expects "a weaker opening based on bond prices, weak overseas performance."
The 30-year Treasury bond was off 22/32 to yield 6.94 percent after Wednesday's close at 6.89 percent.
The S&P 500 future was off 4.45 at 835.50.
